extracted.intended_audience: NIH K99/R00 reviewers and grant applicants (postdoctoral researchers developing intervention pilots)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and documenting a K99/R00 research strategy to develop, pilot, and preliminarily test a culturally inclusive clinician training and PST-based tool for home hospice dementia care, using mixed methods and a staged intervention development framework. Includes aims, methods, sample sizes, analyses, benchmarks, and conduct training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim 1 (K99 Y1) — Identify challenges, strategies, and gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct semi-structured interviews with African American and white family caregivers (FCG) and hospice/palliative clinicians (target: 40 FCG [20 African American, 20 white] and 20 clinicians) to identify the most common and distressing challenges, strategies used, and gaps in care/support for community-dwelling patients with dementia (PwD) nearing end-of-life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews 30–45 min; include current and bereaved FCG; sample until thematic saturation; recruit from VNSNY hospice, WCM-NYP outpatient settings, and community organizations (CaringKind); compare African American vs white FCG and primary vs secondary dementia diagnoses; use findings to guide training/tool content selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim 2 (K99 Y2) — Adapt training materials and develop clinician tool
rubrics_metrics.description: Use stakeholder input and existing literature to adapt culturally inclusive, dementia-focused training materials and create a PST-based goal assessment tool for home hospice clinicians to identify challenges and suggest tailored strategies for PwD and FCG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base training on literature and Aim 1 findings; incorporate cultural inclusivity across sections; provide in-service modules to limit burden; use evidence-based adult education techniques (repetition, case studies, interactive activities); tool provides prompts to identify problems, generate multiple strategies, choose most effective, and create an implementation plan; plan for manualization and digitization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim 3 (R00 Y1) — Feasibility and acceptability testing with iterative revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct two-stage iterative testing with clinicians and FCG to assess and revise training and tool for feasibility, acceptability, usability, and cultural inclusiveness; target total n=50 (training: two groups of 10 clinicians; tool: two groups of 15 including clinicians and diverse FCG).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use interactive sessions, debriefings, 'think aloud' exercises followed by 15–20 min qualitative interviews; evaluate utility of modules, appropriateness, organizational fit, cultural inclusiveness, and usability; modify after each stage to produce final training and digitized tool; expect success if ≥70% endorsement on each feasibility measure (see measures). Use CREATE usability protocols for digitization/usability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim 4 (R00 Y2–Y3) — Pilot randomized test of preliminary efficacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct a pilot cluster-randomized trial with VNSNY hospice clinical teams (40 clinicians in two groups of ~20 each) and enroll ~160 PwD/FCG (4 per clinician; 2 African American, 2 white) to assess preliminary efficacy of training+tool vs usual care on clinician knowledge/confidence, FCG burden (primary), and PwD hospice disenrollment (exploratory).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliver training as in-service sessions; clinicians in intervention use tool across up to four visits and track implementation; assess FCG burden prior to each of 4 visits; verify hospice discharge via electronic records; register pilot RCT on ClinicalTrials.gov; use pilot data to power a future fully-powered RCT (R01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility benchmarks for training/tool success
rubrics_metrics.description: Success of training assessed by 70% or greater endorsement of each feasibility measure; Aim 3 hypotheses expect >70% of home hospice clinicians will (1) complete training, (2) report training/tool are useful, (3) increase knowledge of dementia-related challenges and care strategies, and (4) increase confidence in providing dementia-related care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use participant self-report measures and qualitative feedback; clearly define and report percent endorsement per measure; use these thresholds to judge readiness for pilot testing and revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary and exploratory outcomes specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary outcome for pilot: reduction in family caregiver (FCG) burden (measured via 12-item Zarit Burden Interview [ZBI]). Exploratory outcomes: patient with dementia (PwD) hospice disenrollment rates (lower rates expected in intervention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure FCG burden at baseline and up to three follow-ups (4 total assessments); verify disenrollment via hospice records at 3 and 6 months; include exploratory analyses for racial disparities in outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative analysis and power justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary analysis uses a full information mixed model approach; power calculations based on two-group comparison of endpoint means with adjustment for clustering (design effect), assumed σ2, α=0.05, reliability R, ICC, and cluster size; with n=80 per group can detect moderate effect sizes (Cohen's d ≈ 0.38–0.49) corresponding to ~3.7–4.8 ZBI points depending on correlation between waves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report all assumptions (σ, R, ICC, Nc, ρ), compute variance inflation factor Vif=1+(Nc-1)Icc, and adjust sample size formulas for unreliability; present detectable effect sizes for different correlation scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use validated measures where possible; develop and document new measures when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer validated or objective measures for outcomes; when validated measures do not exist, draw on measures used in literature, published recommendations, or develop tailored measures to be validated in future studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document rationale for measure selection, psychometric properties when available, and plans for future validation; include measurement schedule (see Table 4) and self-report administration details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixed-methods design and qualitative rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a mixed-methods design (qualitative interviews, stakeholder feedback, feasibility testing, and pilot trial). For qualitative analysis, aim for thematic saturation, use responsive interviewing models, independent trained raters, thematic coding, and consensus building.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record and transcribe interviews and focus groups, have multiple coders independently identify passages/themes, organize into categories, discuss and reach consensus on themes, and use identified themes to inform intervention modifications; continue sampling until saturation is reached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder engagement and modified Delphi consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: Use multiple rounds of structured feedback from key stakeholders (hospice clinicians, African American and white FCG, content/research experts) via a modified Delphi approach to develop and refine training and tool content until consensus is reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target 15–20 stakeholders (e.g., 5 clinicians, 5 African American FCG, 5 white FCG, 5 experts); solicit feedback on clarity, relevance, and feasibility; request feedback within 4 weeks and conduct 30–60 minute follow-up interviews; iterate until consensus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usability testing methods: think-aloud and CREATE protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the tool using think-aloud exercises with FCG and clinicians and assess usability in real-world hospice settings using CREATE usability protocols. Digitize final tool using user-centered design and usability standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After think-aloud sessions, conduct qualitative interviews to confirm findings; use CREATE protocols for structured usability assessment and digitization; produce user manuals and digital versions for pilot testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training design and educational techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Design clinician training as in-service modules modeled on programs that increased healthcare worker knowledge and altered practice, incorporating evidence-based techniques: repetitive exposure, case studies, and interactive activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit burden by providing modular in-service sessions during team meetings; include cultural inclusivity as a theme across modules; assess utility of individual modules and organizational fit during feasibility testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling and recruitment standards with attention to diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Recruit purposive samples to achieve racial diversity (equal numbers of African American and white FCG where specified), involve community partners (CaringKind, VNSNY, WCM-NYP), and monitor/adjust recruitment to reach targeted representation (also monitor sex/gender representation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If initial targets are not met, continue recruitment until thematic saturation or engage additional partners and experts in African American recruitment; prioritize recruitment of African American participants when underrepresented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cluster randomization and implementation fidelity
rubrics_metrics.description: Randomly assign clinician teams (clusters) to intervention or usual care to test the training/tool; clinicians in intervention use the tool with enrolled FCG across up to four visits and track implementation of identified strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for clustering in power/sample size calculations and analyses; standardize delivery by providing in-service training; monitor clinician completion rates and fidelity to tool use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical, regulatory, and transparency practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Register pilot RCT on ClinicalTrials.gov and verify self-reported outcomes (e.g., hospice discharge) using electronic hospice records; ensure responsible conduct of research training for investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow institutional and federal policies for human subjects protection; maintain transparency by prospective registration and data verification; include RCR training plans and topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmarks for scholarly productivity and investigator development
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain four peer-reviewed publications directly related to the study (FCG/clinician perspectives; developing training & tool; pilot testing & revisions; preliminary efficacy) and additional dissemination via conferences and local talks; produce data sufficient for a competitive R01 application and for PI to launch as an independent investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track publications and presentations annually; use pilot data to inform a fully-powered RCT proposal and expansion to other settings/populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical constraints, alternatives, and contingency planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge limitations (e.g., excluding PwD from interviews due to reliability concerns, limited budget/time precluding web-based formats) and specify alternative approaches (e.g., consider PwD in future studies, test alternate tool development approaches if needed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide reasoned justification for methodological choices and contingency plans for recruitment, format, or tool approach; describe how pilot data will inform future iterations/scalability.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR training and topics for responsible conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators will complete Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR) courses and CITI human subjects protection training; RCR topics include research misconduct, data management/sharing, animal welfare, human subjects, conflicts of interest, authorship, peer review, mentoring, social responsibility/export control, and rigor/transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain up-to-date certifications (e.g., CITI refresher every 4 years); engage in one-on-one mentor discussions about ethical conduct; document completion dates and ongoing training plans.
